evidence: Pollio in Cic. Fam. 10.32.2 (Lewis & Short): of Gades
terms.comment: Classically the council of any community, not only Rome’s: of Gades and of the Aedui (Lewis & Short), and of the Greek towns of Bithynia in Pliny’s letters to Trajan (Ep. 10.79–80, 112–115). Morgan–Owens gives it for a modern city council, after Milton; senātus mūnicipālis keeps it apart from a national senate.

terms.grammar: noun phrase: senātus with the adjective mūnicipālis

terms.gloss: the councillors of a Roman town
terms.comment: The members of the council of a mūnicipium or colony (Lewis & Short); one councillor is decuriō (Traupman 178, 297). Traupman’s word for a city council.

phrases.latin: nē quis capiat magistrātum nēve sit in senātū minor annōrum trīgintā
phrases.english: that no one under thirty may hold office or sit on the council (in the towns of Bithynia)
